description: CO2-eq burden and cost breakdown for recycling aluminium (remelting scrap) using hydropower electricity, compared against primary production and the current market price. Sourced findings carry their source; conjectures are tagged 'assumed value' with numeric confidence.

triples.name: aluminium recycling

triples.name: secondary aluminium
triples.description: Aluminium produced from scrap by remelting

triples.name: hydropower electricity
triples.description: Electricity generated from hydroelectric plants, used here as the assumed sole electricity source

triples.name: CO2-eq burden
triples.description: Greenhouse gas emissions expressed as carbon dioxide equivalents

triples.name: conversion cost
triples.description: Cost of transforming scrap into finished secondary aluminium, excluding the metal value of the scrap input

triples.name: scrap input cost
triples.description: Purchase cost of aluminium scrap feedstock, indexed to the LME price

triples.name: specific electricity demand
triples.description: Electrical energy required per tonne of output

triples.name: melt loss
triples.description: Material lost as dross and oxidation during remelting, expressed as a mass fraction

triples.name: LME 3-month price
triples.description: London Metal Exchange three-month closing reference price for primary aluminium

triples.name: regional premium
triples.description: Surcharge on top of the LME base for physical delivery, e.g. duty-paid European billet premium

triples.name: gas-fired furnace
triples.description: Remelting furnace heated by natural gas combustion rather than electricity

triples.name: electric furnace
triples.description: Remelting furnace where all process heat is supplied electrically

values.description: Recycling uses about 5% of the energy of primary production (Hall-Heroult ~14,000 kWh/t).
Derived from ~5% of ~14 MWh/t primary; remelting electricity typically 0.6-0.7 MWh/t. Range 0.6-0.7.
Subjective probability that the assumed 0.65 MWh/t is the right value within the range 0.6-0.7.
Hall-Heroult electrolysis requires approximately 14,000 kWh per tonne.
Lifecycle emission factor for hydropower, typical range 10-24 gCO2eq/kWh; midpoint used.
Subjective probability that the assumed 17 gCO2eq/kWh is the right value within the range 10-24.
Hypothetical case: ALL energy electric from hydropower, only material/dross losses remain. Range 50-150 kg/t.
Subjective probability that the assumed 90 kg CO2-eq/t is the right value within the range 50-150.
Electricity-only share at 0.65 MWh/t and 17 gCO2eq/kWh. Range ~7-16 kg/t. Excludes non-electric process emissions.
Subjective probability that the assumed 12 kg CO2-eq/t is the right value within the range 7-16.
Realistic full balance for secondary aluminium with gas-fired remelt furnace. Range ~300-600 kg/t. Contrast to the hydropower electric case.
Subjective probability that the assumed 450 kg CO2-eq/t is the right value within the range 300-600.

source.name: International Aluminium Institute global average (widely cited industry figure)

values.description: Global average primary aluminium footprint. Hydropower-based primary (Norway/Iceland) ~4-6 t/t.
3-month closing price (day-delayed). Down ~12% over the preceding four weeks after Gulf de-escalation; early-June high was 3752 USD/t.

source.name: London Metal Exchange LME Aluminium Alloy

values.description: LME Aluminium Alloy 3-month closing price; cast alloys can trade above primary due to tightness.
Regional premium typically 80-300 USD/t (e.g. ~210 US Midwest, ~180 Japan CIF). Midpoint used.
Scrap typically 70-95% of LME depending on quality. At LME ~3150 that is ~2200-3000 USD/t. Midpoint used.
Subjective probability that the assumed 2600 USD/t is the right value within the range 2200-3000.
Total conversion margin excluding metal value: energy ~40-60, melt loss, labour, salts, pretreatment, maintenance. Range ~150-400 EUR/t.
Subjective probability that the assumed 275 EUR/t is the right value within the range 150-400.
Electricity cost component of conversion: 0.65 MWh/t at ~60-100 EUR/MWh industrial. Small share of total conversion cost.
Subjective probability that the assumed 50 EUR/t is the right value at 60-100 EUR/MWh industrial electricity.
Dross and oxidation loss during remelting, typically 2-8%. Midpoint used; often the largest hidden cost block.
Subjective probability that the assumed 5% melt loss is the right value within the range 2-8%.
